head: claude/mi34-wedge-page-to-digest
title: alarm: a close wedge PROVEN unclearable goes to the digest, not the pager (MI-34)
body:
## What the operator decided

On #10679 / `OI-20260901-ALPACA-SHARE-HOLD-CLASSIFIER-SHIPPED-NOT-YET-OBSERVED`: the `alpaca_paper` GLD close has failed since 2026-08-27 because OCO parent `2e843e04-5487-470c-a702-70e796fbd05e` sits at `pending_cancel` with `canceled_at` null. No bot-side lever clears it. Asked what the alarm should do meanwhile, the operator chose **"downgrade to the daily digest."**

**This PR is alarm ROUTING only.** It does not touch a close path, the classifier, the order path, or the live wedge — that is #10679's, and it needs operator/venue action.

## The class is narrow, and that is the whole design

The downgrade keys on `share_hold == broker_cancel_wedged` — an **evidenced determination** `classify_share_hold()` makes by reading the residual order's own `status` from the broker (#10679, already on `main`). **There is no retry count anywhere in the new module**, and a test pins that structurally via AST, so the module's own prose about streaks cannot satisfy it.

A close failing for an **unknown** reason pages exactly as before, however many times it repeats. Five parametrised tests assert that for every other reading — including `residual_unreadable` ("we could not look at the broker") and `not_classified` ("nobody classified it at all").

## Five transitions, one quiet

`close_wedge.transition`, registered with `collapsed-state-guard`:

| transition | routes |
|---|---|
| `newly_wedged` | **PAGES** — downgrading the *arrival* would hide the condition, not de-noise it |
| `still_standing` | **the one downgraded state** — carried in the digest |
| `evidence_changed` | **PAGES** — a second, unexamined fault must not inherit the first's suppression |
| `cleared_confirmed` | **PAGES** — attributed, and only reachable from the monitor's confirmed-close path |
| `vanished_unattributed` | **PAGES** — the position is gone and nothing explains it |

`LOUD_TRANSITIONS` is the **complement** of the quiet state, so a transition added later is loud by default.

`vanished_unattributed` is its own state deliberately. A position that simply disappears is not a clean clear — `PROTECTION_REASSERT_MODE` is the precedent (a gate at `annotate` with an empty allowlist got read as having fixed a divergence it could not have touched), and this OI row names the same trap in its own `clears_when`.

## Silence is not reachable

This was the operator's own stated risk — the item falling quietly out of **both** channels. Four independent things prevent it:

1. **`still_standing` is floored, not silenced.** One page per `CLOSE_WEDGE_REPAGE_HOURS` (default 24h), down from the close-failure backoff's hourly cap — so the change is ~24 pages/day → 1, not → 0.
2. **Suppression is conditional on the carry.** A failed ledger write, an unreadable ledger, or a raise anywhere in the router all page. A downgrade whose carry fails is a deletion, and this refuses to be one.
3. **The digest renders the block in all three read states and none is empty.** An un-fetched ledger says *"NOT EXAMINED … this is 'we did not look', NOT 'nothing is wedged'"*. Self-test 14 asserts no reachable state renders silence, and **fails under a surgical break** (verified: 4 injected breaks, 4 caught).
4. **The floor does not depend on the digest working at all** — which matters, because the digest's renderer was dropping queued bodies until #10747 landed this morning, and `probes.yml`'s first-ever scheduled run came **~4h50m late** against a daily cron.

## Was `_append_operator_alert` the right seam?

**Right for the RECORD, insufficient for the DELIVERY** — so both halves are done.

- **Record:** the ring row is written on **both** routes, carrying `route`. `operator_alerts` is the only surface a page rate is recoverable from; dropping the row with the ping would make *"we downgraded it"* and *"it never fired"* identical **there**, destroying the one instrument that answers the desensitised-alarm question. CLAUDE.md now warns not to compute a rate over `close_failure` without splitting on `route`.
- **Delivery:** the digest runs on a GitHub runner and `runtime_logs/` is `.gitignore`d and VM-local, so it could not see the ledger at all. New path: allowlisted on diag **in the same commit as its writer**, and `work-digest.yml` fetches it.

## A defect the tests caught, not shipped

`sweep_vanished` persisted its clock only when it retired something. Every quiet pass therefore discarded the evidence that we *had* been watching, pinning `last_sweep_at` at the last re-arm — which made `vanished_unattributed` **unreachable in production** while every unit test of the retirement logic passed. Now persisted every pass; the test fails if reverted (verified).

The sweep also refuses to conclude anything on a pass whose own last run is older than the window: *we were not looking* is not *it went away*, so a trader that was down does not wake up and page a flood of false disappearances.

## Also

`share_hold.state` is registered with `collapsed-state-guard` too — it now **gates an alarm**, and a state that gates an alarm must be enforced as one. Its four readings gained a real consumer (`_share_hold_guidance`): before this, every "won't flatten" page said *"investigate the venue/connection"* whether a retry was about to work, provably never would, or we had failed to look at the broker. `not_classified` is deliberately **not** a declared state (the producer cannot emit it — it is a fact about our coverage), following the `trainer_disk_unknown` reasoning.

Two CLAUDE.md/register corrections are included and called out in their own commits: the OI row's "NOT MERGED" half was false (#10679 **is** on `main`, verified by `git merge-base --is-ancestor`), and three of my own citations of the never-fired-on-cron row went stale when #10753 cleared it mid-branch.

## Verification

- **53 of 53 relevant guards pass** (`run_guards.py --base main`), `collapsed-state-guard` clean at **27 contracts** (up from 25).
- **28 new tests**; **1189 passed / 0 failed** across the touched surfaces (`-k "close or diag_unit or operator_alert or alpaca or notification or collapsed"`).
- Import layering verified separately: **6 contracts kept, 0 broken** (`run_guards` reported 127 for `layer-guard` because `lint-imports` is not installed in my container, not a violation).
- **Not observed on the fleet.** No live wedge has been seen flowing through this, and the digest has never been observed carrying one. Both are deployment facts, not test facts, and the floor exists precisely because neither has happened yet.
